mock_data.title: A Lucky Escape
mock_data.passage:
Several people had a lucky escape yesterday while waiting for a bus at the corner of King Street and George Street. Some scaffolding fell from a building and landed just behind them. Fortunately, no one was injured because there is a stretch of grass around the front of the building and most of the scaffolding landed on it.

'The bits of the scaffolding landed too close for comfort,' said 66-year-old Bert Thomson. 'It's a miracle no one was hurt, but we were all in shock. You don't expect to dice with death when you're waiting for a bus. I hope the town council are going to do something about this.'

'I absolutely agree,' said 56-year-old Margaret Simpson. 'None of us got hit by the scaffolding, but the fact of the matter is that it was a very narrow squeak and I'll be contacting the council. They shouldn't allow dangerous things like that on buildings. It wasn't even windy when the stuff fell down. Make no mistake, if the council don't do something soon, it'll happen again and other people might not be so lucky.'

A council representative said later, 'We are all very sorry to hear of this unfortunate accident, but it is not the fault of the council. Responsibility for maintaining such scaffolding rests fair and square with the contractor who erected it. Anyone who is concerned about this incident should contact the contractor directly.'

Later in the day, some local residents who live in the vicinity of the building in question contacted us to give their views. 'This was an accident waiting to happen,' said their spokesperson, 50-year-old Tom Scott. 'It has been a bone of contention between the council and ourselves for quite some time. The scaffolding is in a poor state of repair and no one has worked on the building for several weeks. Not only did we think it was potentially dangerous, but it's a real blot on the landscape. They should be made to finish the work and take the scaffolding down. At the end of the day, the council have a moral responsibility to keep the town safe for their residents. As far as people in this area are concerned, the council must carry the can. They've been putting the whole issue on the back burner for too long.'

mock_data.passageC1:
Bystanders experienced a close call yesterday at the intersection of King Street and George Street as scaffolding unexpectedly collapsed from a nearby building, landing mere inches behind where they were waiting for a bus. A fortuitous patch of grass surrounding the building's facade served as a buffer, preventing what could have been a far more tragic outcome, and miraculously, no injuries were sustained.

'The debris landed uncomfortably close,' recounted Bert Thomson, 66. 'It’s nothing short of a miracle that no one was hurt; we were all understandably shaken up. One doesn't anticipate courting danger while simply waiting for public transport. I sincerely hope the town council will take decisive action to address this.'

Margaret Simpson, 56, echoed this sentiment, stating, 'While we all managed to dodge a bullet, the reality is that it was an exceedingly near miss, and I intend to lodge a formal complaint with the council. They cannot condone such hazardous conditions on building sites. The weather was benign when the scaffolding gave way. Let there be no ambiguity: unless the council gets its act together, a recurrence is almost inevitable, and future incidents might not be so benign.'

A council spokesperson later issued a statement: 'We deeply regret this unfortunate incident; however, the council is not culpable. The sole responsibility for the maintenance of such scaffolding rests squarely with the contractor responsible for its erection. Any individuals with concerns regarding this incident should liaise directly with the aforementioned contractor.'

Later that day, local residents residing in the immediate vicinity of the building in question contacted us to voice their concerns. 'This was a foreseeable accident,' asserted their spokesperson, Tom Scott, 50. 'The dilapidated state of the scaffolding has been a source of contention between residents and the council for a considerable period. Construction on the building has been suspended for several weeks, exacerbating the situation. Not only did we consider it a potential hazard, but it also constitutes a significant eyesore. The authorities should compel the completion of the works and the removal of the scaffolding. Ultimately, the council bears a moral obligation to ensure the safety of its residents. As far as the local community is concerned, the council must shoulder the blame for this debacle. They have consistently kicked the can down the road on this issue for far too long, and now we see the consequences.'

mock_data.translation:
Kecha bir necha kishi King ko'chasi va Jorj ko'chasi burchagida avtobusni kutayotganlarida omadli qochib qutulishdi. Binoning iskalasi yiqilib, ularning orqasiga tushdi. Yaxshiyamki, hech kim jarohatlangan emas, chunki binoning old tomonida o't maydoni bor va iskalaning ko'p qismi unga tushdi.

"Iskalaning bo'laklari juda yaqin tushdi, qo'rqinchli edi", dedi 66 yoshli Bert Tomson. "Hech kim jarohatlanmagani mo'jiza, ammo biz hammamiz hayratda qoldik. Avtobus kutayotganingizda o'lim bilan o'ynashni kutmaysiz. Umid qilamanki, shahar kengashi bu haqda biror narsa qiladi."

"Men butunlay qo'shilaman", dedi 56 yoshli Margaret Simpson. "Hech birimiz iskalaga uralib qolmadik, ammo gap shundaki, bu juda tor qochish edi va men kengashga murojaat qilaman. Ular binalarda bunday xavfli narsalarga ruxsat bermasliklari kerak. Narsalar tushganida hatto shamol ham yo'q edi. Xato qilmang, agar kengash tez orada biror narsa qilmasa, bu yana sodir bo'ladi va boshqa odamlar shuncha omadli bo'lmasligi mumkin."

Kengash vakili keyinroq dedi: "Biz hammamiz bu baxtsiz hodisadan xafa bo'ldik, ammo bu kengashning aybi emas. Bunday iskalani saqlash mas'uliyati uni o'rnatgan pudratchi zimmasida to'g'ridan-to'g'ri. Bu hodisadan xavotirda bo'lgan har kim to'g'ridan-to'g'ri pudratchiga murojaat qilishi kerak."

Kun davomida keyinroq, ko'rib chiqilayotgan bino atrofida yashovchi ba'zi mahalliy aholi o'z fikrini bildirish uchun bizga murojaat qildilar. "Bu sodir bo'lishini kutayotgan baxtsiz hodisa edi", dedi ularning vakili 50 yoshli Tom Skott. "Bu ancha vaqtdan beri kengash va o'zimiz o'rtasida tortishuvli masala edi. Iskala yomon holatda va bir necha hafta davomida binoda hech kim ishlamadi. Biz uni potentsial xavfli deb o'ylaganimizgina emas, balki u haqiqatan ham manzarada dog'. Ular ishni tugatishga va iskalani olib tashlashga majbur qilinishi kerak. Oxir-oqibat, kengash aholi uchun shaharni xavfsiz saqlash bo'yicha axloqiy mas'uliyatga ega. Bu hududdagi odamlar uchun kengash javobgarlikni o'z zimmasiga olishi kerak. Ular butun masalani juda uzoq vaqt davomida chetga surib qo'yishdi."

mock_data.translationB1:
Kecha ba'zi odamlar avtobusni kutayotganda omadli qutulishdi. Ular King Street va George Street ko'chalarining burchagida edilar. Bir binodan o'rmon qulab tushdi. Ular orqasiga tushdi. Yaxshiyamki, hech kim jarohatlanmadi. Chunki binoning oldida o't bor edi. O'rmonning ko'p qismi o'tga tushdi.

66 yoshli Bert Thomson shunday dedi: "O'rmon juda yaqin joyga tushdi. Hech kim zarar ko'rmagani mo'jiza edi. Hammamiz juda hayratda edik. Avtobus kutayotganda bunday narsa bo'lishini o'ylamaysiz. Umid qilamanki, shahar kengashi bu borada biror narsa qiladi."

56 yoshli Margaret Simpson ham baxtsiz hodisa haqida gapirdi. "Men qo'shilaman", dedi u. "Bizga o'rmon tegmagan. Ammo bu juda xavfli vaziyat edi. Men kengash bilan bog'lanaman. Ular binolarda bunday xavfli narsalarga ruxsat bermasliklari kerak. U qulaganda hatto shamol ham yo'q edi. Agar kengash tez orada biror narsa qilmasa, bu yana takrorlanishi mumkin. Va boshqa odamlarning omadi kelmasligi mumkin."

Kengash a'zosi keyinroq shunday dedi: "Biz bu baxtsiz hodisa haqida eshitganimizdan afsusdamiz. Ammo bu kengashning aybi emas. O'rmonni nazorat qilish pudratchining mas'uliyati. Agar kimdir xavotirda bo'lsa, ular to'g'ridan-to'g'ri pudratchi bilan bog'lanishlari kerak."

O'sha kuni keyinroq yaqin atrofda yashovchi ba'zi odamlar biz bilan bog'lanishdi. 50 yoshli Tom Scott ular nomidan gapirdi. U shunday dedi: "Bu baxtsiz hodisa bo'lishi kerak edi. Biz bu borada kengash bilan uzoq vaqtdan beri bahslashib kelmoqdamiz. O'rmonning ahvoli yomon. Bir necha haftadan beri binoda hech kim ishlamadi. Biz buni xavfli deb o'yladik. U juda xunuk ham ko'rinadi. Ular ishni tugatib, o'rmonni olib tashlashlari kerak. Kengashning shaharni xavfsiz saqlash mas'uliyati bor. Kengash aybni o'z zimmasiga olishi kerak. Ular bu muammoga juda uzoq vaqtdan beri e'tibor bermayaptilar."
mock_data.translationB2:
Kecha King Street va George Street burchagida avtobus kutib turgan bir necha kishi xavfdan arang qutuldi. Yaqin atrofdagi binodan qurilish iskala qulab tushib, ular turgan joyning orqasiga tushdi. Yaxshiyamki, hech kim jarohat olmadi, chunki bino atrofida o'tloqli maydon bor edi va iskala asosan shu yerga tushdi.

'Iskala juda yaqin joyga tushdi,' dedi Bert Thomson, 66 yosh. 'Hech kimga zarar yetmagani - bu omad kulib boqishi, lekin biz hammamiz juda qo'rqib ketdik. Jamoat transportini kutib turganingizda hayot uchun xavfli vaziyatda bo'lishni kutmaysiz. Umid qilamanki, mahalliy kengash bu borada chora ko'radi.'

'Men butunlay qo'shilaman,' deya qo'shdi Margaret Simpson, 56 yosh. 'Garchi hech birimizga iskala bevosita tegmagan bo'lsak ham, bu juda mo'jizaviy qutulish bo'ldi. Men kengash bilan bog'lanmoqchiman. Ular binolarda bunday xavfli inshootlarga ruxsat bermasliklari kerak. U qulagan paytda ob-havo tinch edi. Ishonchingiz komil bo'lsin, agar kengash tez orada bunga e'tibor qaratmasa, bu yana sodir bo'lishi mumkin va boshqalarning omadi kelmasligi mumkin.'

Kengash vakili keyinroq shunday dedi: 'Bu noxush voqea haqida eshitganimizdan juda afsusdamiz. Biroq, kengash bunga javobgar emas. Iskalani saqlash bo'yicha butun mas'uliyat uni o'rnatgan pudratchiga yuklatiladi. Bu voqea haqida xavotirda bo'lgan har bir kishi to'g'ridan-to'g'ri pudratchi bilan bog'lanishi kerak.'

O'sha kuni binoga yaqin joyda yashovchi mahalliy aholi o'z fikrlari bilan bo'lishish uchun biz bilan bog'lanishdi. 'Bu sodir bo'lishi kutilgan baxtsiz hodisa edi,' dedi ularning vakili Tom Scott, 50 yosh. 'Bu biz va kengash o'rtasida bir muncha vaqtdan beri bahsga sabab bo'lib kelayotgan masala. Iskala yomon ahvolda va bir necha haftadan beri binoda hech kim ishlamayapti. Biz buni nafaqat potentsial xavfli, balki ko'zni qamashtiruvchi deb hisobladik. Ulardan ishni tugatish va iskalani olib tashlash talab qilinishi kerak. Oxir oqibat, kengash o'z aholisining xavfsizligini ta'minlash uchun axloqiy majburiyatga ega. Bu yerdagi aholining fikricha, kengash javobgarlikni o'z zimmasiga olishi kerak. Ular bu masalaga juda uzoq vaqtdan beri e'tiborsizlik qilib kelishmoqda.'

Kengash vakili keyinroq bayonot berdi: 'Biz bu baxtsiz hodisadan chuqur afsusdamiz; ammo, kengash aybdor emas. Bunday iskalaga xizmat ko'rsatish uchun yagona mas'uliyat uni o'rnatgan pudratchiga **yuklanadi**. Ushbu hodisa yuzasidan xavotirlari bo'lgan har qanday shaxs bevosita yuqorida aytilgan pudratchi bilan bog'lanishi kerak.'
